mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in three of the last four weeks (-26.3, -35.3, -30.1, -35.6) with the most recent week at the series low. This momentum reflects ongoing suppression of discretionary shopping and leisure trips that will persist into the next four weeks absent a reversal signal.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at t-0w (-35.6) is the lowest value in the four-week window
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean despite the series showing a declining or flat trend in the final two observed weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has risen steadily (5.3, 9.1, 7.0, 10.0) indicating increasing stay-at-home behavior consistent with tightening movement restrictions. Once RESIDENTIAL sustains above +9.5 points, retail footfall is mechanically constrained further as households substitute home-based activity for outings, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean exceeds +9.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 10.0 at t-0w, its highest value in the window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks even though RESIDENTIAL remains above +9.5 points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-10.4 to -23.4) and WORKPLACES (-17.6 to -26.3) have both declined sharply over the same period as RETAIL_REC. Reduced commuting and workplace attendance jointly remove incidental retail stops (lunch, errands, transit-adjacent shopping), compounding RETAIL_REC decline beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both series declined in parallel with RETAIL_REC across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next two weeks while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain jointly depressed or continue declining together.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC, PARKS, and TRANSIT all show synchronized declines over the last two observed weeks, a pattern typical of escalating movement restrictions being implemented or anticipated. This broad-based co-movement signals an active tightening regime that will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: at least three of RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES decline simultaneously for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC, PARKS and TRANSIT all reached their lowest or near-lowest values at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC trends upward over the next four weeks despite continued simultaneous decline in PARKS and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed near baseline (ranging -7.6 to +3.9) even as RETAIL_REC fell sharply, showing households substitute essential-only trips for discretionary retail visits. This substitution pattern indicates continued avoidance of non-essential retail activity in the near term.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fluctuates near zero while RETAIL_REC stays deeply negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable near baseline, breaking the expected substitution linkage.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS decline (-21.4 to -31.1) may partly reflect seasonal heat onset in Delhi during April rather than policy restriction, since outdoor leisure naturally drops as temperatures rise independent of retail mobility. If this seasonal effect dominates, RETAIL_REC need not continue falling in lockstep with PARKS and could mean-revert upward as the policy-driven component is overstated.
candidate_trigger: PARKS continues declining while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stabilize or flatten
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -31.1 at t-0w, its lowest point, while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showed smaller relative declines
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to fall in parallel with PARKS over the next four weeks, indicating the decline is policy-driven rather than seasonal.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has oscillated rather than monotonically declined (-26.3, -35.3, -30.1, -35.6), suggesting a bounce-back pattern where sharp drops are followed by partial recovery. This oscillation implies the next week is likely to see a rebound similar to the t-1w recovery from the t-2w trough.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rebounded from -35.3 at t-2w to -30.1 at t-1w before falling again to -35.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rebound and instead sets a new low in the week immediately following t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL combined with falling WORKPLACES jointly indicate a shift toward enforced home confinement rather than voluntary caution. When both series move together in this direction, the combined effect historically compounds RETAIL_REC suppression more than either series alone, reflecting active lockdown-style policy enforcement.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 10.0 while WORKPLACES fell to -26.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers over the next four weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues rising and WORKPLACES continues falling together.
